items.stem: Arjun, a farmer, sells wheat worth ₹700 to a flour mill. The mill sells the flour to a biscuit company for ₹900. The company sells biscuits to consumers for ₹1,700. What is the contribution of these transactions to GDP? Why are the earlier values not added?
items.answer: ₹1,700; adding wheat and flour would be double counting since they are intermediate goods
items.markingKey: Only the value of the final good counts: ₹1,700 (1 mark). Value added: ₹700 + ₹200 + ₹800 = ₹1,700 (1 mark). Adding ₹700 + ₹900 + ₹1,700 = ₹3,300 would count wheat and flour more than once (1 mark).

items.stem: Riya, a farmer, sells wheat worth ₹1,100 to a flour mill. The mill sells the flour to a biscuit company for ₹1,700. The company sells biscuits to consumers for ₹2,900. What is the contribution of these transactions to GDP? Why are the earlier values not added?

items.markingKey: Only the value of the final good counts: ₹2,900 (1 mark). Value added: ₹1,100 + ₹600 + ₹1,200 = ₹2,900 (1 mark). Adding ₹1,100 + ₹1,700 + ₹2,900 = ₹5,700 would count wheat and flour more than once (1 mark).

items.stem:
(a) Explain with an example how the three sectors depend on one another. (3 marks)
(b) Why is the tertiary sector also called the service sector? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) A farmer grows sugarcane (primary). (2) A sugar mill buys it to make sugar (secondary). (3) Trucks, banks and shops help the sugar reach consumers (tertiary). (4) A strike by transporters would affect both farmers and mills. (b) (1) Its activities do not produce a good themselves. (2) They are aids or supports for the production process.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) A farmer grows sugarcane (primary). (2) A sugar mill buys it to make sugar (secondary). (3) Trucks, banks and shops help the sugar reach consumers (tertiary). (4) A strike by transporters would affect both farmers and mills. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Its activities do not produce a good themselves. (2) They are aids or supports for the production process.

items.stem:
(a) Explain the role of the public sector in the economic development of a country. (3 marks)
(b) Why does the government sell electricity and water at low rates? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) It provides infrastructure such as roads, bridges, railways and ports. (2) It supplies electricity and water at low cost. (3) It ensures health and education for all. (4) It buys grains at fair prices and sells them through ration shops. (b) (1) Many small industries and the poor cannot afford high rates. (2) The government bears part of the cost to promote public welfare.
